name: MonarchAiLauncher
title: AiLauncher
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.FloatingActionButton and ExtendedFloatingActionButton (solid), androidx.compose.material3.Button (subtle), androidx.compose.material3.BadgedBox with Badge
summary: The button that opens and closes an AI assistant: a round floating action button or a quieter toolbar button, with an unread dot, a count or a working ring.
whenToUse: As the one entry point to an assistant on a screen: in the floatingActionButton slot of a Scaffold, or in a toolbar or navigation rail.
whenNotToUse: For the main action of a screen that is not the assistant use a FloatingActionButton or MonarchButton. Inside the assistant panel use its own close control.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiLauncher(open: Boolean, onOpenChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, icon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAiLauncherVariant = MonarchAiLauncherVariant.Solid, badge: MonarchAiLauncherBadge? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, showLabel: Boolean? = null, closeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, label: String? = null, badgeLabel: String? = null, openLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
sealed interface MonarchAiLauncherBadge { data object Unread; data object Working; data class Count(val count: Int) }

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the assistant the launcher controls is open.

options.name: onOpenChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the user activates the button.

options.name: icon
options.description: The assistant glyph. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: variant
options.description: Solid: a round, filled floating action button with the medium shadow. Subtle: a tinted button with its label for a toolbar.

options.name: badge
options.description: Unread (a dot), Working (a ring) or Count(n).

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can activate the launcher.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Shows the label beside the icon. null shows it for the subtle variant only.

options.name: closeIcon
options.description: Replaces icon on the solid variant while the assistant is open.

options.name: badgeLabel
options.description: Replaces the spoken text of the badge.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the interactions of the button.

states.name: open
states.description: The solid variant shows closeIcon, when given, instead of icon; the subtle variant's border takes the solid assistant color.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The solid variant takes the active assistant fill and the subtle variant the hovered-subtle assistant fill.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The muted fill and the disabled text color; the click is ignored and the button is exposed as disabled.

states.name: unread
states.description: A dot in the solid danger color at the top end corner.

states.name: working
states.description: Half of the outline, in the thinking assistant color, travels around the button. With animations off the whole outline is drawn and still.

states.name: count
states.description: The number at the top end corner, "99+" above 99, nothing for zero or less.

appearance: Solid: the solid assistant fill with the on-solid assistant content color and the medium Monarch shadow. Subtle: the subtle assistant fill, the strong assistant content color and the assistant border. Badges use the solid danger fill. The same roles apply in light, dark and high contrast.
platformNotes: The parity map listed this entry as style (a themed FloatingActionButton with BadgedBox); it is built as a wrapper, as on iOS, because the open state, the spoken badge and the working ring are behavior the theme cannot give a plain FloatingActionButton. The web positions the launcher (bottom-end, bottom-start, inline) and moves it above other floating elements; on Android the app places it, usually in the floatingActionButton slot of a Scaffold, so there are no position or avoid parameters. The web's global Ctrl/Cmd+J shortcut is not offered: Compose has no window-wide key listener a component can own, so an app that wants it handles the key in onPreviewKeyEvent at the root of the screen and calls onOpenChange. Material 3 floating action buttons have no disabled state, so a disabled solid launcher ignores clicks and is marked disabled for TalkBack. The badge has no ring in the surface color as on the web.
accessibility: A button whose content description is "Assistant", or label.
Its state description is "Open" while open, followed by the badge: "New messages", "Working" or "3 unread messages", so nothing rests on the dot alone.
The icon and the badge are hidden from TalkBack as separate elements.
Both variants reserve a 48dp touch target.
The working ring stands still when the user has turned animations off.
The badge sits at the top end corner, which mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: The count text uses a plural resource for one and for more; languages with more forms are covered by the plural resource or badgeLabel.
The badge stands outside the button's corner; leave room around it.
The working ring is drawn 2dp outside the button and is not clipped by the component.

examples.title: Inline (rail) launcher
examples.template:
MonarchAiLauncher(
    open = open,
    onOpenChange = { open = it },
    variant = MonarchAiLauncherVariant.Subtle,
    showLabel = true,
    label = {{label}},
)
examples.code:
MonarchAiLauncher(
    open = open,
    onOpenChange = { open = it },
    variant = MonarchAiLauncherVariant.Subtle,
    showLabel = true,
    label = "Assistant",
)

examples.title: A subtle launcher in a toolbar
examples.code:
MonarchAiLauncher(
    open = false,
    onOpenChange = {},
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Bot, contentDescription = null) },
    variant = MonarchAiLauncherVariant.Subtle,
)
